text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-9876 - gpu_alloc_fail cluster-west2a (severity: P1)

ashley (oncall): acked the PD incident, oncall handover in progress. seeing repeated CUDA OOM logs across multiple pods in gateway-gpu-pool.

drew: seeing the same. High alloc failures from model-serve-legacy v2. Quantizing jobs + some large batching spikes. Customer-facing 5xx for ~7% of inference requests for customer-ids: cust_omega, cust-beta.

katie: can we triage which jobs are holding most vram? running `kubectl top pods -n inference | sort -r -k3 | head` now.

hamid: quick dump from node gpu-12: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] model-serve-legacy-5f6c8 - CUDA Error: out of memory when allocating 2147483648 bytes
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] kvcache: failed to allocate slab 0x7f2b... errno=12
[2026-03-15T09:12:07Z] eviction: triggered preemptive reclaim, but active tasks prevent reclaim
```

ashley (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale down heavy-batch deployments 2) cordon and drain any node showing repeated alloc fails 3) route traffic to dedicated fallback model variant (smaller) 4) escalate to L2+ (hamid) if OOMs persist after draining. doing 1 now.

drew: taking traffic off model-serve-legacy via routing rule: `redwoodctl routes update inference --match model=legacy --weight 0.2` (lowered to 20%). will monitor 60s.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-9876 acknowledged by ashley (oncall) at 2026-03-15T09:13:12Z. Escalation scheduled in 10m.

katie: snapshot of top memory consumers (post-rate-limit): ```
NAME                                   MEMORY( Mi )
model-serve-legacy-5f6c8              11365Mi
batch-prep-2b9f1                       8423Mi
customer-job-cust_omega-0              6021Mi
```

hamid: batch-prep is suspicious; it's doing large dynamic batches for experimental pipeline. I'm pausing batch-prep job for now: `kubectl scale deploy batch-prep --replicas=0 -n inference` -> paused.

ashley (oncall): cordoning node gpu-12 and draining non-critical pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` in progress.

drew: routing change showing drop in alloc failures after 90s. telemetry: alloc_fail rate down from 13/min to 2/min. customer 5xx rate down to 1.1%.

support-lead: opened a short status note to affected customers (cust_omega, cust-beta) — telling them we are mitigating and will update in 30m.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-9876 escalated to L2 (hamid) at 2026-03-15T09:23:12Z.

hamid: looking into memory fragmentation metrics; kv-cache evictions spiked. Found one long-running tenant job pinned to certain GPU memory ranges. Killing that job freed ~5.5Gi.

katie: after killing tenant job and draining node, free memory stable. Trace: ```
free_gpu_mem before: 1.2Gi
free_gpu_mem after: 9.1Gi
alloc_fail count: 0 in the last 2m
```

ashley (oncall): moving to containment -> drafted rollback playbook: revert heavy-quantized rollout, permanently disable batch-prep for next 6 hours, add auto-evict threshold to 70% usage.

drew: rebalanced traffic fully to primary pool; monitoring 10m. no new PD pages in last 8m.

ashley (oncall): PD-INC-9876 status update: mitigated, customers have reduced errors, continued monitoring. preparing handoff to daytime oncall at 2026-03-15T10:00Z.

support-lead: customer impact summary for postmortem: 
- root cause: memory fragmentation + an unbounded dynamic-batching job (batch-prep) + heavy legacy model memory usage
- scope: ~7% error rate at peak, impacted two mid-tier customers for ~18 minutes
- mitigation: paused batch-prep, drained one noisy node, killed pinned tenant job, traffic reroute to smaller model variant
- next steps: add kvcache auto-compact, set batch-prep quota, add eviction SLO and alert to warn at 60% instead of 80%

hamid: leaving notes on the incident ticket PD-INC-9876. assigning follow-ups to eng-runtime (kvcache compaction) and eng-platform (auto-evict rules).

ashley (oncall): handing off to @drew for wound-down monitoring. full incident thread saved to the incident tracker. closing Slack thread after handoff. :white_check_mark:
